sections.h2: Which offices handle a Woodbridge tax bill?
sections.html:
A Woodbridge bill passes through three public offices. The Assessor values the parcel, the Tax Collection Office issues the bill and takes the money, and the Middlesex County board listens to owners who dispute the value. Woodbridge collects everything, then forwards the county's share.

Woodbridge property tax errands and the office for each
OfficeHandlesAddress, phone, hours
Township Tax AssessorSetting each parcel's value, new construction included, and administering tax appealsMunicipal Building, 1 Main Street, Woodbridge 07095. Phone 732-602-6002
Tax Collection OfficeBilling and payment for property tax and for water and sewerFirst floor of Town Hall, 1 Main Street. Open Monday to Friday from 8:30 a.m., closing at 4:30 p.m. except Tuesday at 6:30 p.m.
Middlesex County Tax BoardCertifying assessments and ruling on appealsCounty Administration Building, 4th floor, New Brunswick 08901. Phone 732-745-3350. Open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. until 4:15 p.m.

The Assessor must hold a state certification. The Tax Board serves all 25 municipalities in the county.

Taxes arrive in four quarterly installments dated February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, and the township mails bills only twice a year, in January and July.

Sewer runs on its own track. The second-half sewer bill is due October 1, and what counts is the day the township receives payment, with no credit for a postmark. Your own stub shows the exact dates.

When a closing falls close to an installment date, call the collector's office and ask how a late payment would be handled.

Woodbridge accepts payment five ways.

  • Online, through the Taxpayer Information site. Search for your property, choose Make Payment, and follow the prompts. Electronic checks add $1.95, and cards add roughly 2.95 percent.
  • At the counter on the first floor of Town Hall with cash, a check or a money order.
  • In the drop-off box outside Town Hall.
  • By mail to P.O. Box 5004, Woodbridge, NJ 07095, with the check payable to Township of Woodbridge.
  • Through ACH direct withdrawal, using separate forms for tax and sewer.

Tuesday is the late evening at the counter. A seller clearing a balance just ahead of the deed will likely find online payment or a certified check at the window the fastest.

Disputes over value are not decided at Town Hall. Petitions go to the county tax board through its online portal, my.njappeal.com. You set up a login there and may upload evidence until seven calendar days before the hearing, by 4:00 p.m.

Two cutoffs apply. A petition on an added or omitted assessment has to reach the board in person by 4:15 p.m. on December 1, shifting to the next business day if that is a weekend or holiday. An owner denied a senior or disabled deduction files Form A-1 by the following April 1.

For a routine appeal, the board at 732-745-3350 can tell you the deadline that matches your notice. When an appraiser's report is offered in an added or omitted case, the appraiser has to testify in person.

An owner who is 65 or older, or disabled, may take $250 off the annual bill after a year of New Jersey residence. The rules also look at ownership and occupancy on October 1 of the pretax year, an on-time application and an income limit.

  • Form PTD plus proofs goes to the township assessor or collector.
  • Form PD5 renews the deduction by March 1 each year.
  • A surviving spouse or civil union partner aged 55 or older can continue it on the same home.
  • The township's Tax Collector page carries a veteran deduction form.

State Property Tax Relief filing events are run by the Division of Taxation in Trenton, so ask the Division when the next one is.

Before you sign a contract, ask the Tax Collection Office to put the balance on your block and lot in writing. A mid-quarter closing leaves part of a period to divide, and you should ask how a late payment would be credited.

Put the receipts for recent quarters in the closing folder. Sewer follows its own calendar, so it needs a separate figure, and the buyer's closing agent will ask for both. If you believe the assessment is off, raise it with the Assessor at 732-602-6002 before you list.

Anything unpaid is deducted from your proceeds when you close. A cash buyer taking the house as is can close quickly, yet still needs the same payoff numbers, so ask for them the day a closing date is set.

The 2020 census recorded 103,639 people in Woodbridge, and the latest estimate is 104,802. No separate towns exist inside it. The township is a patchwork of Avenel, Colonia, Fords, Hopelawn, Iselin, Keasbey, Menlo Park Terrace, Port Reading, Sewaren and Woodbridge proper. Your mailing name may be any of these, yet the township bills the tax for every one.

Close to a fifth of the township lies in FEMA flood hazard areas, and tides have repeatedly flooded land by the Woodbridge River, the Raritan at Keasbey and the Arthur Kill at Sewaren and Port Reading. A house in those spots should come with its flood insurance policy and any elevation certificate.

The median owned home is worth $433,000, median gross rent is $1,959, and about two of every three homes are lived in by their owners. Commuters have Turnpike Exit 11, the Parkway and NJ Transit stops at Metropark, Avenel and Woodbridge.

sections.h2: What a buyer will ask about
sections.html:
Expect the buyer's side to request the latest bill, proof of payment for each quarter and the sewer statement. They may also ask whether an appeal is pending, since a reduction granted after closing can change what the new owner pays. If you filed a petition, tell your attorney so the contract can say who benefits. Deductions do not transfer automatically, so a buyer who is 65 or older or disabled will need to apply on their own forms.

If the house is in a flood area, buyers and lenders also look for the insurance paperwork, so having it on hand speeds things up.

1. Phone the collector and request tax and sewer balances in writing.
  2. Check the account for a senior, disabled or veteran deduction.
  3. Ask the Assessor if work you did triggered an added or omitted assessment.
  4. File your recent quarterly receipts together.
  5. Pass both balances to the closing agent for the current-quarter split.

Every item takes one call or one Town Hall visit. Finishing them before listing protects your closing date. If a mortgage escrows your taxes, also ask the lender what it has paid, so nothing is counted twice when the closing agent splits the quarter.

faqs.q: When do Woodbridge property taxes come due?
faqs.a: Installments are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1. Bills go out in January and July.

faqs.q: Where can I pay a Woodbridge tax bill in person?
faqs.a: Use the Tax Collection Office on the first floor of Town Hall. Cash, checks and money orders are accepted, and the counter runs late on Tuesdays.

faqs.q: What does it cost to pay a Woodbridge bill online?
faqs.a: An electronic check costs $1.95. A credit or debit card costs roughly 2.95 percent of the payment.

faqs.q: Which body decides a Woodbridge assessment appeal?
faqs.a: The Middlesex County Board of Taxation decides it. Use the board's online portal, or call 732-745-3350 for guidance.

faqs.q: Does Woodbridge have a senior tax deduction?
faqs.a: Yes, a $250 annual deduction for qualifying owners 65 or older or disabled. File Form PTD to start it and Form PD5 by March 1 each year to keep it.
